title: Staged rollback and tenant-priority recovery playbook for mixed-hosting model regressions
creator: Aria Chen
description: Create an operational playbook and lightweight orchestration helpers to perform tenant-prioritized, staged rollbacks across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments when a model rollout shows regression signals in canary slices. Focus is on minimizing customer impact, reconciling per-tenant KV cache/state, and providing clear customer communication and remediation SLAs.
problem_statement: Recent incidents showed mixed-deployment rollouts can leave tenants in inconsistent inference states (stale/poisoned KV cache, model mismatch across routes) after partial rollbacks. Current ad-hoc remediations are slow, error-prone, and lack tenant-prioritization semantics for paid/dedicated customers.
goals: Define an operator-friendly staged rollback sequence that works across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private control planes
Add lightweight orchestration primitives to pause traffic slices, reconcile KV caches or evict prefixes, and perform differential rollback where necessary
Provide a clear customer-facing timeline and escalation script for SRE/CS to use
Automate safe-rollforward path (reapply patch) for tenants that require fast restore rather than full rollback
acceptance_criteria: Runbook documented and reviewed by Oncall, SRE, and PM
Orchestration helper scripts (kvcache-evict, slice-pause, staged-traffic-shift) merged to infra repo with tests
Playbook exercised during 1 scheduled fault injection test (chaos) for Hosted and Dedicated staging environments
Customer comms templates validated with CS and Legal for dedicated/private SLAs
runbook_steps: 1) Detect: alerting thresholds (quality/regression) trigger incident — annotate affected model version and tenant slices
2) Classify: quick triage to confirm regression (perf/quality/latency) and list impacted tenants (priority by contract tier)
3) Quarantine: pause new traffic to failing canary slices via route-level feature gate (non-destructive)
4) KV reconciliation: run kvcache-verify to compare active prefix footprints; for poisoned prefixes run kvcache-evict <tenant, prefix> or shadow-evict to measure impact
5) Staged rollback: perform a 3-step rollback per-slice — a) revert canary slice model, b) run smoke generation against tenant prompts, c) gradually shift traffic back if checks pass
6) Tenant-priority path: for P1/P0 customers, offer accelerated path: pin tenant to a stable model variant and perform live prefix invalidation rather than full infra rollback
7) Observe: enforce short-run quality evals (prompt set) and token-level latency/cost checks for the tenant and global rollouts
8) Communicate: send templated updates to affected customers at T+30m, T+2h, T+24h or until resolved
9) Postmortem: capture timelines, root cause, and recommended runtime instrumentation changes (e.g., per-tenant delta metrics)
communication_plan: Initial triage: private Slack channel + incident bridge; SRE posts assessment to account CS lead
Customer-facing: standardized template — summary, immediate mitigation, ETA for next update; tailor for Dedicated/Private contractual notes
Post-resolution: executive summary with impacted tenant list, severity, and compensation/credits path (if applicable)
risks_and_tradeoffs: Aggressive kvcache eviction reduces chances of sticky regressions but can increase cold-start latency for heavy tenants
Tenant-prioritized paths can delay a global rollback; we accept temporary heterogeneity to preserve SLAs for high-value customers
Automated staged shifts reduce human error but require robust canary signal thresholds to avoid oscillation
